blocks.text: RIYADH, Saudi Arabia — The Saudi capital’s tallest skyscraper was struck for a second time in days on Tuesday, injuring 11 people, as the coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis denounced what it called a “terrorist attack.” Three separate witnesses said the strike targeted the 80-story Public Investment Fund Tower, which houses the kingdom’s sovereign wealth fund and dominates Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD). The building was attacked last Thursday and is one of several high-profile targets hit since hostilities with the Iran-backed Houthis resumed in July. “One of the towers in the financial center was targeted in a cowardly terrorist attack,” […]...
